newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS prices rise on lower U.S. inventories.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS prices rise on lower U.S. inventories.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices rose solidly Thursday during ACCESS, supported by depletions in U.S. petroleum and refined products supplies, traders said.
Crude oil for February delivery erased daytime losses by climbing 25 cents overnight to $25.17 a barrel. About 915 lots traded in the front-month contract and 1,600 overall.
Prices got a lift from a weekly inventory data which showed U.S. supplies of crude oil down 5.2 million barrels last week.
The report, released late Thursday by the American Petroleum Institute (API), an industry trade group, also reported a 1.8 million draw in distillate stocks.
Heating oil, a type of distillate, rose 0.59 cents a gallon in the January contract to 70.65 cents. Volume in early overnight trade stood at 124 lots for January and 175 total.
Front-month gasoline rose 0.44 cents to 69.95 cents a gallon, as 55 lots traded in January.
